**[Oculoid](oculoid.html)** plays a free CC BY 4.0 textured eye inside a spherical
chrome-or-brown shell. Independently moving eyelids, swept lashes, vessels,
a dilating pupil and a corner-anchored tear turn glances into short squishes
and lid gestures into plops. Tear releases one growing drop; Cry repeats at its
own tempo even with Motion stopped. Poke with adjustable diameter and depth,
stretch the eyeball, or shine a variable-width flashlight
to constrict its pupil. Retract the lids or hide the whole shell; switch
between a textured or black 3D globe, or pack 1–12 globes into the
same sheath. Two to four retain touching formations; larger groups stack
at several depths. Banter, Harmony and Rock out give each eye its own
moving, short stereo voice while the shared eyelids play an independently
paced rhythm. Wardrobe props shape the next eye or lid hit without starting
a sustained sound. Dress the eyelids with a cigar, mustache, lipstick, teeth,
tongue, a woven scarf, open coat or workout headband; add 3D aviators,
cat or human ears, a furry tail, customizable bow tie, mullet, mom bob,
top/cowboy hat, frosting, cherry or a sitting cat. Pick a reflective eyelid
color, polka dots on lids, iris or
eyeball, and stripes or concentric bands on the globe. An X/Y gaze pad,
movable lights and a chrome reflection knob,
independent repeating eyeball and eyelid animations with their own dice,
and 36 full musical presets provide varied looks
and movements. Audio starts off; a resting eye is quiet. Find it in Work in Progress.
[Controls, asset provenance and limits](docs/oculoid.md).

## Oculoid eye model

Oculoid includes the textured globe and separate iris meshes from
**Realistic Human Eye** by **DEGUIDER**, licensed under
[CC BY 4.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/).
[Original Sketchfab model](https://sketchfab.com/3d-models/realistic-human-eye-b68ae822b45443edb812950993ece362).
The unchanged GLB was retrieved via Objaverse. Morphazoid rotates and scales
it at runtime and adds authored, deforming eyelid/skin geometry, eyelashes,
vessels, a pupil, glints, lighting and playable sound. The catalogue icon is
a render of this adapted model. These additions are artistic approximations,
not medical anatomy or an endorsement by the original artist. Download link,
license, changes and SHA-256 are in `assets/oculoid/SOURCE.LICENSE.txt`.

The falling teardrop adapts geometry from **CC0 - Drops** by **plaggy**:
[original Sketchfab model](https://sketchfab.com/3d-models/cc0-drops-f8f24228aebf41f297c878ad82ea7db0).
Despite the title, the GLB's embedded license is **CC BY 4.0**, not CC0.
The bundled GLB retains the teardrop positions, normals and triangles while
removing source textures and materials. At runtime a copy is tilted away
from the lid, with a new water material, growth from the lower lid corner
and a vertical fall.
Original and derivative hashes, source credit and extraction instructions are in
`assets/oculoid/SOURCE.LICENSE.txt`. Neither creator endorses Morphazoid.

Oculoid's aviator sunglasses use **Aviator sunglasses** by **Kimppo**,
[CC BY 4.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/):
[original Sketchfab model](https://sketchfab.com/3d-models/aviator-sunglasses-00d1cb5aa82745228a3b764c97f867de).
The unchanged GLB includes its upright FBX conversion. At runtime its width
and temple depth are fitted to the lid, a visible brow bridge is added, its
lenses are darkened, and the pair follows the upper lid.
See `assets/oculoid/SOURCE.LICENSE.txt` for the mirror, hash and exact changes.
Kimppo does not endorse Morphazoid.

# Catalogue logo generation

## Oculoid

`oculoid.webp` is a 512 × 512 WebP render of Oculoid's own WebGL eye:
the rounded eyelid edges and unsquashed spherical shell use the default
neutral mirror-chrome finish (warm brown is selectable on the page).
The black socket sits behind
the globe, not on the lid rim. There is no flat background oval, tear duct
or extra lower-lid crease.
The browser loaded DEGUIDER's [CC BY 4.0 eye](../oculoid/SOURCE.LICENSE.txt)
with Morphazoid's authored lids, lashes, vessels and pupil. At a 1440 × 900
desktop viewport, take a 1× DPR canvas screenshot (1050 × 767 pixels), crop
`(141, 0, 908, 767)` to exclude the heading and keep the full orb, then
resample to 512 pixels with Lanczos and save as WebP at quality 90. No added
oval, vignette, generated replacement anatomy or unrelated photograph was used.
